doc.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Guitar duets with Joe Pass and the Donte's club
summary: They first played together at Donte's in Los Angeles and packed the place; Pass was the best soloist and accompanist.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: When did it occur to you to start doing these great duet records with other guitar players?
Gosh. Well I first did them with Joe Pass. And I don’t know how that came about. But we both played Donte’s in Los Angeles you know, at different times.
It was the name of a club. So one time we decided to play together. And we packed the place. So after that when we played, we played together.
I’m always curious about how two chordal instruments communicate when you’re playing a tune, when you decide to go somewhere else with it.

Well that’s the secret — I mean it’s not a secret — I mean it’s just kind of you either have that or you don’t have it. And Joe was the best soloist of course. And then the best accompanist that I’ve ever had. He knew just when to play something and just when to lay out. And hopefully I’m pretty good at that too.
That idea of when to lay out is really important.
Very important. Well see Joe listens to what everyone else is playing.
